claims.claim: Spark RDDs are immutable partitioned datasets with lineage-based recomputation; transformations are lazy and actions trigger execution.
claims.notes: RDD and DataFrame APIs have different execution details, but both expose distributed execution concepts.

claims.claim: Spark shuffle redistributes records across partitions so values with the same key can be co-located; it can incur network, serialization and disk I/O costs.
claims.notes: The cost depends on data volume, partitioning, storage and the query plan.

claims.claim: Spark SQL Adaptive Query Execution can coalesce post-shuffle partitions and optimize skewed shuffle joins using runtime statistics.
claims.locator: Adaptive Query Execution; Coalescing Post Shuffle Partitions; Optimizing Skew Join
claims.notes: AQE behavior and configuration are Spark-version dependent.

claims.claim: Reliable Spark RDD checkpointing writes to the configured checkpoint directory and removes references to parent RDDs; localCheckpoint uses executor-local storage and sacrifices fault tolerance.
claims.notes: Do not confuse checkpoint with cache/persist or localCheckpoint.

claims.claim: Ray Data streaming execution lets downstream operators start before upstream operators complete, processes streams of blocks, and uses backpressure to avoid scheduling into backpressured operators.
claims.locator: Execution → Streaming execution and Scheduling loop
claims.notes: Execution details and memory behavior are version-specific; current docs consulted are Ray Data 2.60.

claims.claim: Ray Data map_batches uses stateless Ray tasks for functions and stateful Ray actors for callable classes, supporting persistent model workers for batch inference.
claims.locator: map_batches description and stateful transform example
claims.notes: Actor pool size, batch size and resource requests must match model memory and cluster capacity.

claims.claim: Ray Data offline batch inference supports job-level checkpointing so reruns can skip records already processed under the same checkpoint configuration.
claims.notes: Checkpoint support is workflow/API-specific and does not make arbitrary external side effects exactly-once.

claims.claim: Stable partition identifiers, immutable shard outputs and a validated final manifest are a practical way to make retried data-processing tasks idempotent.
claims.locator: RDD lineage and recomputation semantics; engineering recommendation
claims.notes: Exactly-once external writes still require a sink-specific commit protocol or idempotency key.
